concepts.name: Microglial cells
concepts.rationale: Microglia are the primary immune cells in the CNS, and their dysfunction is thought to contribute to neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease. Single-cell RNA sequencing can provide insights into microglial heterogeneity and identify novel biomarkers for this disease.
freetext: Microglia are the resident immune cells of the central nervous system (CNS) and play a crucial role in maintaining brain homeostasis.
In Alzheimer's disease, microglial activation is thought to contribute to neurodegeneration by releasing pro-inflammatory cytokines and promoting neuronal damage.
Single-cell RNA sequencing has emerged as a powerful tool for studying microglial heterogeneity and identifying novel biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease.

concepts.name: Alzheimer's disease
concepts.rationale: Alzheimer's disease is a complex neurodegenerative disorder with a multifactorial pathogenesis. Single-cell RNA sequencing can provide insights into the heterogeneity of microglia in different stages of the disease.
freetext: Alzheimer's disease is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline and memory loss.
The pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease involves the accumulation of amyloid-beta plaques and tau protein tangles, leading to neuronal damage and death.
Mitochondrial dysfunction is thought to contribute to the progression of Alzheimer's disease.

concepts.name: Single-cell RNA sequencing
concepts.rationale: Single-cell RNA sequencing is a powerful tool for studying the heterogeneity of single cells. This technique can provide insights into microglial biology and identify novel biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease.
freetext: Single-cell RNA sequencing is a powerful tool for studying the heterogeneity of single cells.
This technique involves the analysis of RNA sequencing data from individual cells to identify unique gene expression profiles.
Single-cell RNA sequencing has emerged as a key component in understanding complex biological systems, including microglia in Alzheimer's disease.

concepts.name: MicroRNA
concepts.rationale: MicroRNAs are small non-coding RNAs that regulate gene expression by binding to mRNA. In Alzheimer's disease, microRNAs have been shown to play a role in regulating cellular stress responses and promoting neuronal survival.
freetext: MicroRNAs are small non-coding RNAs that regulate gene expression by binding to messenger RNA (mRNA) and preventing its translation.
In Alzheimer's disease, microRNAs have been shown to play a role in regulating cellular stress responses and promoting neuronal survival.
MicroRNAs can also be used as biomarkers for diagnosing and monitoring the progression of neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's.

concepts.name: mRNA
concepts.rationale: mRNA is the primary transcript in eukaryotic cells, responsible for encoding proteins. In Alzheimer's disease, mRNA has been shown to play a role in regulating cellular stress responses and promoting neuronal survival.
freetext: mRNA is the primary transcript in eukaryotic cells, responsible for encoding proteins.
In Alzheimer's disease, mRNA has been shown to play a role in regulating cellular stress responses and promoting neuronal survival.
mRNA can also be used as biomarkers for diagnosing and monitoring the progression of neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's.

concepts.name: Transcriptomics
concepts.rationale: Transcriptomics is the study of the complete set of RNA transcripts in a cell or organism. In Alzheimer's disease, transcriptomics has been shown to provide insights into microglial heterogeneity and identify novel biomarkers for this disease.
freetext: Transcriptomics is the study of the complete set of RNA transcripts in a cell or organism.

concepts.name: Microglial cells
concepts.rationale: Microglia are the primary immune cells in the CNS, and their dysfunction is thought to contribute to neurodegeneration in Alzheimer's disease. Single-cell RNA sequencing can provide insights into microglial heterogeneity and identify novel biomarkers for this disease.
freetext: Microglia are the resident immune cells of the central nervous system (CNS) and play a crucial role in maintaining brain homeostasis.
In Alzheimer's disease, microglial activation is thought to contribute to neurodegeneration by releasing pro-inflammatory cytokines and promoting neuronal damage.
Single-cell RNA sequencing has emerged as a powerful tool for studying microglial heterogeneity and identifying novel biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease.

concepts.name: Alzheimer's disease
concepts.rationale: Alzheimer's disease is a complex neurodegenerative disorder with a multifactorial pathogenesis. Single-cell RNA sequencing can provide insights into the heterogeneity of microglia in different stages of the disease.
freetext: Alzheimer's disease is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline and memory loss.
The pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease involves the accumulation of amyloid-beta plaques and tau protein tangles, leading to neuronal damage and death.
Mitochondrial dysfunction is thought to contribute to the progression of Alzheimer's disease.

concepts.name: Single-cell RNA sequencing
concepts.rationale: Single-cell RNA sequencing is a powerful tool for studying the heterogeneity of single cells. This technique can provide insights into microglial biology and identify novel biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease.

This technique involves the analysis of RNA sequencing data from individual cells to identify unique gene expression profiles.
Single-cell RNA sequencing has emerged as a key component in understanding complex biological systems, including microglia in Alzheimer's disease.

concepts.name: MicroRNA

MicroRNAs can also be used as biomarkers for diagnosing and monitoring the progression of neurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's.
